title: Business Discovery Framework

stages.name: Understand the request
stages.objective: Understand what the customer is asking for and why.
stages.exit_rule: The requested outcome can be restated without inventing facts.

stages.name: Understand the business
stages.objective: Understand the business model, audience, offering, and operating context.
stages.exit_rule: Material business context is recorded with its evidence status.

stages.name: Define the problem
stages.objective: Distinguish the underlying problem from the proposed solution.
stages.exit_rule: The problem statement is supported by customer input or explicitly provisional.

stages.name: Define objectives
stages.objective: Establish intended business outcomes and their measures.
stages.exit_rule: Each major objective has an owner or an identified ownership gap.

stages.name: Discover stakeholders and users
stages.objective: Identify decision-makers, affected teams, users, and relevant needs.
stages.exit_rule: Critical stakeholder groups and decision authorities are identified or flagged.

stages.name: Discover requirements
stages.exit_rule: High-priority requirements have acceptance criteria or explicit gaps.

stages.name: Discover constraints and dependencies
stages.objective: Identify factors that constrain or block implementation.
stages.exit_rule: Critical dependencies and implementation blockers are recorded.

stages.name: Prioritize scope
stages.objective: Establish priorities, trade-offs, and release boundaries.
stages.exit_rule: Priority decisions have an identified decision owner and rationale.

stages.name: Validate the discovery record
stages.objective: Check accuracy, contradictions, missing evidence, and approvals.
stages.exit_rule: The next-stage readiness decision is documented.

operating_rules: Stages may iterate when new information appears.
Discovery depth must be proportional to project complexity and risk.
Do not treat a proposed solution as proof of the underlying problem.
Do not convert an AI recommendation into an approved customer requirement.
Critical unknowns may block specific decisions without blocking all discovery work.
